title: The largest first-ever payments
question: Which payees received the most in the first year the City ever paid them, how was that money awarded, and what became of them?
finding: From fiscal 2020 to 2026, 164 payees received $1 million or more in the first year they appear in the ledger, $660.1 million in all; 34% of that first-year money is recorded as competed and 16% under a rule that sets competition aside (2020: 31%, 2021: 38%, 2022: 26%, 2023: 9%, 2024: 5%, 2025: 4%, 2026: 12%). The largest: PRG-Potrero Properties LLC ($65.0 million in fiscal 2026, all under a rule that does not say); Granite Construction Company ($58.6 million in fiscal 2026, all competed); City Gardens Bridge LLC ($46.9 million in fiscal 2023, all under a rule that does not say). Of the 164 listed, 54 grew, 37 stayed about the same, 16 shrank, 35 vanished and 22 are too new to say.
how: A payee’s first year is the first fiscal year in which any payment to it was issued, looking back to fiscal 2017. The year is read from the voucher number, not from the year the file lists the line under, so a payee whose lines sit under a later year but were issued in fiscal 2018 or earlier is not new. The table lists every publicly identifiable payee meeting the first-year threshold in each year from 2020 to 2026, counting outside spending only. "How awarded" reads the purchasing rule keyed on the first-year payments. Afterwards: "grew" if any later year reached one and a half times the first; "shrank" if no later year reached half; "vanished" if no payment of any kind appears in the last two fiscal years or in fiscal 2027 to date.
limits: A large first payment is usual for a joint venture formed for one construction project, a new landlord, the one-time purchase of a building, a bulk purchase of buses or computers, and anything bought under the pandemic emergency of fiscal 2020 to 2022. A firm that was renamed or bought appears as new. Housing loans, which go to a new partnership for each building, are left out altogether. What would settle a row: the solicitation and the award memo for that first contract. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. The $992.6 million of outside spending that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier is in none of the figures here; it is used only to tell that a payee is not new.
